samples.question: The picture has three parts on a cream background. At the bottom is a track of seven coloured square cells in a row; each cell is one of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, brown or teal. Exactly one cell carries a black ring, and that is the cell the marker starts on. Directly above the track is one row of coloured circles and no triangles: that row is the programme, read from left to right. Above the programme are three legend rows. Each legend row begins with one coloured circle, called a badge, followed to its right by one, two or three dark triangles. Every circle in the programme has the same colour as exactly one legend badge and stands for that legend row's triangles; a programme circle is never a move by itself. Carry out the programme one circle at a time from left to right: for each programme circle take the triangles of the legend row with the matching badge colour, in left-to-right order, and for each triangle move the marker one cell to the right if that triangle points right and one cell to the left if it points left. The same legend row may be used more than once, the order in which the legend rows are drawn does not matter, the track does not wrap, and the marker never leaves the track. What is the colour of the cell the marker finishes on?
